clue.text: Perhaps he has, the spirit to break the law!

definitions.text: Perhaps he has, the spirit to break the law!

parts.words: Perhaps he has, the spirit to break the law
parts.note: read as a person with a bold spirit of lawlessness, but the spirit is liquor carried illegally, as in Prohibition-era smuggling

explanation.surface: A daring rebel seems to have the temperament for lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like character or nerve; it is alcohol, and the man breaks the law by selling or smuggling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler or illicit seller of liquor carries spirits and breaks the law doing so.

clue.text: Stupid, though having many degrees

definitions.meaning: an angle wider than ninety degrees, short of a straight line

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person, though they hold a string of university qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' suggests academic qualifications; it means degrees of angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: slow on the uptake, and in geometry an angle of more than ninety degrees.

clue.text: Cake is the wrong one-upset everyone

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the wrong cake was served and everyone is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican cake of maize or wheat flour.

clue.text: Makes clear a sloppy clue -one on fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it
sloppy means done carelessly, so the letters of the word clue are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
dates are a fruit

explanation.surface: A solver complains about a careless clue, with a fruit thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' rearranges CLUE to ELUC; 'on' puts I above DATES in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to explain or throw light on something.

clue.text: Depart -on an old sort of boat

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another comes above it

parts.note: to go is to depart

indicators.note: sort of signals the words are reworked into a different form

explanation.surface: Someone leaves on an old-fashioned kind of boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges AN OLD to NDOLA, which follows GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the long flat-bottomed Venetian boat rowed with one oar.

clue.text: 10 : Nonsense !

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, read as two words, is an instruction: take the word star and turn it round, which describes how the letters here were made

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 10's answer is two words: STAR, then TURN, telling you to turn STAR back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of contempt or disbelief, like rubbish or bosh.

clue.text: A trifle irritating

parts.note: read as slightly annoying, but it describes a tiny itchy bite from a small jumping insect, a trivial nuisance

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bite from a small parasite, and figuratively any minor annoyance.

clue.text: Illusory discoveries of Sterne MSS--a revised version

indicators.note: a revised version of a text is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scholars claim false finds in a revised edition of Laurence Sterne's manuscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised version' rearranges STERNE MSS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a supposed discovery that turns out to be imaginary.

clue.text: Lamb announces identity of Fielding's girl

parts.note: saying who one is: I am ...
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer reveals who Henry Fielding's heroine really is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb announcing his identity says 'I AM ELIA'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is the heroine of Henry Fielding's 1751 novel of that title.

clue.text: Best performer opening-gets run out

parts.note: a start is an opening

indicators.note: out signals the word run is put out of order

explanation.surface: The leading performer gets run out at the start of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RUN to URN. 'Run out' looks like cricket, where a batsman is dismissed, but it is fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The star turn is the main or most impressive act in a show.

clue.text: Sid retires with girl shame!

indicators.note: retires means draws back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Grace is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Sid withdraws with a girl in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns SID into DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace is loss of honour or reputation.

clue.text: Inventor of a literary pen, name ?

definitions.meaning: Alexander Graham ..., inventor of the telephone
the Bronte sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton, sharing one surname

explanation.surface: Someone asks who invented a writer's pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks who invented a pen-name; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: Alexander Graham Bell of the telephone, and the surname the Bronte sisters wrote under.

clue.text: Vegetarian banquets ?

parts.note: read literally as feasts of beans, but the compound means a festive meal or annual works outing

explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is British slang for a celebration or an employer's annual dinner for workers.

clue.text: The giving of powers to this mission

definitions.meaning: a group of envoys sent to represent others

explanation.surface: A diplomatic mission is handed authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the handing over of authority, and a body of representatives sent abroad.

clue.text: Repellent woman and author found on board

parts.note: a gorgon is a frightening, repulsive woman, from the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth
Emile Zola, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A repulsive woman and a writer are discovered aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on board' suggests a ship's passengers; the board is a cheeseboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese, served on a cheeseboard.

clue.text: Poor Dan backed mount-rather slow

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the name is jumbled
backed means turned backwards, so the volcano's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Mount Etna is the Sicilian volcano

explanation.surface: Poor Dan's horse goes backwards and is rather slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DAN to AND; 'backed' turns ETNA into ANTE. 'Mount' looks like a horse; it is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Animal with a little sleeping place on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another comes above it

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a sleeping room, its name made little by shortening
the Ouse is a common English river name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A creature with a tiny bed set beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the shortened word DORM for dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small rodent famous for its long hibernation.

clue.text: Garments to fit chest ?

parts.note: read as tops sized for the torso, but the chest is a chest of ... and the garments are knickers

explanation.definitionFit: Drawers are old-fashioned underpants, and also the sliding boxes that fit a chest of furniture.

clue.text: Bird taken as fieldfare ?

definitions.meaning: a small migratory songbird with a white rump
read as food from the field: a head of grain

explanation.surface: A bird is mistaken for a fieldfare, a kind of thrush.
explanation.walkthrough: A fieldfare is itself a bird, which makes the second half look like another bird; split it as field fare, the produce of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the wheatear is a songbird, and an ear of wheat is food grown in a field.

clue.text: An old satyr, unless I err

indicators.note: to err is to go astray, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Someone identifies an ancient satyr, adding they may be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'err' rearranges UNLESS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Silenus was the elderly drunken satyr who tutored Dionysus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Enlargement of coffee centre bar sign

definitions.text: Enlargement of coffee centre bar sign

parts.words: Enlargement of coffee centre bar sign
parts.note: the centre of coffee is ff, the sign written in a bar of music for very loud; writing that abbreviation out in full enlarges it

explanation.surface: A café's central counter is getting a bigger sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a bar of music, not a counter, and 'Enlargement' means expanding an abbreviation into the full Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo, very loud, is abbreviated ff in a musical score.

clue.text: Periods in which we are over-assessed ?

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Taxpayers grumble about times when they are charged too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the hyphen of 'over-assessed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long periods of history.

clue.text: What's done in battle

definitions.meaning: fighting, as in killed in combat

explanation.surface: A question about what soldiers do in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a deed performed, and military combat, as in 'killed in' it.

clue.text: Girl in island retreat could be very much loved

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
retreat means go back, so the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl at an island hideaway might be greatly cherished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns ELBA into ABLE; 'in' puts DORA inside it. 'retreat' looks like a hideaway noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means lovable, deserving deep affection.

clue.text: Drink for an existentialist ?

parts.note: a philosopher of existence is concerned with being, so is one who is

explanation.definitionFit: Beer is a drink brewed from malt and hops, and split it reads as one who exists.

clue.text: Modern sort of Eton boy

indicators.note: sort of signals the word is reworked into another form

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A new type of Etonian schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ETON to NEOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoteric is a literary word for recent or newfangled.

clue.text: Sent one a new decoction

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into something different

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone was sent a freshly brewed infusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SENT, I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, an infusion or decoction of leaves or flowers.

clue.text: Where " they also serve

parts.note: Milton wrote that they also serve who only stand and wait; the place is where people wait at tables

explanation.definitionFit: An eating house is where waiters stand and wait, serving diners.
